sentences.text: Now the differences in vessels and lights.
Constrained by draft exists only in International rules.
A vessel pushing ahead shows a sternlight under International rules, but two yellow towing lights Inland, and the barge she pushes carries a special flashing yellow light Inland.
On the Great Lakes, an all-round white light may replace the after masthead light and sternlight.
On the Great Lakes and Western Rivers, a downbound vessel with a following current has right of way, and a vessel crossing the river keeps clear.
Inland, a vessel under twenty meters in a special anchorage area needs no anchor light, and a motorsailing vessel under twelve meters needn’t show the cone.
Inland also adds the flashing white distress light.
